sources.title: Prostitution, Race, and Politics: selected publisher preview
sources.citation: Philippa Levine, Prostitution, Race, and Politics: Policing Venereal Disease in the British Empire (Routledge,2003), publisher preview: acknowledgments ix, introduction7 and10–11, chapter1,15–17.

verification.note: Fresh selected reading of the ordinary public Pageplace publisher preview,50 PDF leaves. Copyright/title pages identify Routledge2003 and the author; acknowledgment dated January2003. Printed ix,11 and16 visually collated. The separate2000article Hall passage16,Poovey17 and note8/references19 are also visually collated in their own PDF; do not transfer these article page numbers to this book. Credits Burton, Epstein and Peers with reading the entire manuscript and arguing its points; uses Hall, Wolfe, Gregg and Said in the specified passages. Preview omits the relevant back-of-book endnote bodies, so exact cited editions/titles are not guessed. Complete monograph and cited originals unread; family, hospitality and musical-support credits are not intellectual arrows.

sources.title: Is Comparative History Possible? — authorial abstract
sources.citation: Philippa Levine, “Is Comparative History Possible?”, History and Theory53(3),October2014,331–347, doi10.1111/hith.10716; first online2October2014.

verification.note: Fresh official publisher authorial abstract and metadata read. It combines the promise of comparison with warnings about universal standards and treating nations as fixed units. Full article body unavailable: the CUNI teaching URL returned a course-unavailable HTML page, not a PDF; publisher full-text link redirected to abstract. Indexed references to particular historians remain discovery leads only. Do not claim full article reading or a personal relationship from its bibliography.

hc177_levine_article.note: Fresh selected primary rereading on 2026-10-28 extends the earlier opening: printed 6,16–21 and corresponding references in the public 19-leaf scan. Explicit uses of Appadurai, Foucault terminology and Catherine Hall are distinguished from missing-endpoint resources. The conclusion on printed17 qualifies Poovey’s definition-before-enumeration proposition in colonial practice; neither the original Poovey essay nor the other cited original books was read. Existing gender and racial-formation claims remain exact, with their original geographical limits.

ch_jbs_response_2003.note: Fresh browser reading on 2026-10-28 of Hall’s selected 533–534 and536–537. Hall explicitly attributes questions about her narrative split and women’s relative absence to both Philippa Levine and Thomas Holt; her reply defends the separated narrative and masculine focus while acknowledging more could have been done with women. This is a recipient’s own account, not a fresh reading of the commentators’ original 505–529 discussion. Local PDF request returned403; actual browser-rendered passages are preserved separately. No earlier reading qualification is removed.
